title: Perioperative enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab for cisplatin-ineligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer
population: 344 patients with operable MIBC who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy
summary: Perioperative enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab improved 2-year EFS (74.7% vs 39.4%), 2-year OS (79.7% vs 63.1%) and pCR (57.1% vs 8.6%) compared with immediate cystectomy.
criticalReview: The magnitude of benefit is clinically important and led to FDA approval in the cisplatin-ineligible perioperative setting. The regimen carries substantial toxicity; discuss neuropathy, rash, hyperglycaemia, immune-mediated adverse events and surgical fitness. Do not derive NNT from hazard ratios or mix this comparison with EV-304 or NIAGARA.

absoluteEffect.toxicity: Clinically important toxicities include peripheral neuropathy, rash, hyperglycaemia and immune-mediated adverse events; page-level grade-specific figures should be consulted.
absoluteEffect.nnh: Not added here because a single verified fixed-time toxicity endpoint was not specified in the prior record.
